title: Pick-Reason Provenance on Every Claim
executive_summary: Extend the existing stampClaim() writer to carry a pick_reason (score, components, comparator version) on every claim, make it QF-aware, and prove chairman-label provenance never alters qf-gated-hold.cjs's exclusion.

functional_requirements.description: Extend the entry built at claim-stamp.cjs:59-62 with pick_reason: {score, components, comparatorVersion}. Resolve the scoring function through an injectable seam mirroring resolveMergeFn (claim-stamp.cjs:41-44) -- e.g. resolveScoreFn(computePriorityScoreFn) that defaults to an optional dynamic import of lib/priority/comparator.cjs. TESTING-AGENT FINDING (evidence e21a99e7): a bare try/catch around a static/dynamic require of a not-yet-existing module path throws at RESOLUTION time in vitest, before any vi.mock can intercept it -- an injectable function parameter is the only way AC-1's numeric-score branch gets real test coverage before Child B (the comparator) merges to main. When no scoring function is available/injected, or its output has no numeric score, pick_reason.score MUST be the literal string 'UNSCORED', never a fabricated 0. No changes to CLAIM_HISTORY_CAP (20) or existing entry fields (session_id, claimed_at, identity_source).
functional_requirements.requirement: stampClaim() in lib/fleet/claim-stamp.cjs writes a pick_reason field on the claim_history entry it already appends, via an injectable scoring seam.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A claim written through claimGuard(), tryClaim() (worker-checkin.cjs), sd-start.js, or session-conflict-checker.mjs produces a claim_history entry whose newest element has a pick_reason object; a unit test injects a fake computePriorityScoreFn to cover the numeric-score branch (Child B's comparator.cjs need not exist for this test to pass).

AC-2: When no scoring function is available (default path, comparator.cjs absent), pick_reason reads {score: "UNSCORED", components: {}, comparatorVersion: null} and stampClaim still returns non-null (fail-soft, not fail-open-to-throw). A NaN or thrown value from an injected scoring function must also degrade to UNSCORED, never propagate NaN/null into components.

AC-3: The 3 existing unit suites referencing claim_history entries (claim-identity.test.js, same-turn-next-claim.test.js, claim-stamp-concurrent-metadata-race.test.js) pass unmodified — pick_reason is additive, asserted via toMatchObject/targeted-key checks, not toEqual on the full entry. (Corrected count: 3 suites, not 4 — testing-agent evidence e21a99e7.)

functional_requirements.description: TESTING-AGENT FINDING (evidence e21a99e7, BLOCKING, now resolved): the originally-proposed 5th positional parameter for table/kind COLLIDES with claim-stamp.cjs's existing 5th parameter, mergeMetadataKeysFn (the injectable merge seam 8 existing test call sites across 3 files already depend on) -- inserting a kind param there breaks that injection and reaching the REAL mergeMetadataKeys in a unit test returns {merged:false} (stubbed pg creds), producing a confusing null. CORRECTED APPROACH: auto-detect the QF shape via a /^QF-/ test on sdRef, matching the existing repo idiom (directed-assignment.cjs:212, dispatch.cjs:348/:468, release-work-item.mjs:133) -- no signature change to stampClaim's existing 4 production call sites. For a QF-shaped ref, attempt an additive JSONB merge onto quick_fixes.metadata via a NEW, separate CAS-guarded merge function (mirroring safe-metadata-merge.mjs's removeMetadataKeyIfClaimedBy pattern: an explicit WHERE claiming_session_id = $sessionId guard, since no generic quick_fixes JSONB-merge helper exists in the repo). This new function must accept its own injectable seam (e.g. mergeQfMetadataFn) so it is unit-testable without a live quick_fixes.metadata column. Detect Postgres error 42703 specifically and return null without throwing -- and TR-3 (below) requires this to be a NAMED, narrow catch, not the existing blanket catch{return null} at claim-stamp.cjs:74-76, which currently makes every stampClaim failure mode indistinguishable and would make TR-3 unverifiable.
functional_requirements.requirement: stampClaim() auto-detects a QF-shaped ref (/^QF-/) and, for that shape, writes to quick_fixes.metadata when present, degrading fail-soft (no-op, no throw) when absent.
acceptance_criteria: AC-4: With quick_fixes.metadata ABSENT (today's live schema), a QF self-claim through worker-checkin.cjs selfClaimQuickFix succeeds end-to-end and the QF-side merge returns null with no thrown error and no test failure.

AC-5: A unit test injects a fake mergeQfMetadataFn to assert a pick_reason-bearing entry is written additively (existing metadata keys preserved) under a claiming_session_id compare-and-swap guard, without requiring a live quick_fixes.metadata column.

AC-6: worker-checkin.cjs's tryClaim (the single choke point at :394, already used by selfClaimQuickFix at :765) is the only stamping call site needed to cover all 3 previously-named QF-id lanes (critical-qf-jump.cjs:113 and directed-assignment.cjs:270 both funnel through tryClaim, confirmed by testing-agent evidence e21a99e7 — they do not need separate edits). Evidence for this AC must be collected from a test file NOT in tests/quarantine-manifest.json (tests/unit/worker-checkin-critical-qf-priority-jump.test.js is quarantined and excluded from the unit project; use tests/unit/claim-liveness-fence-qf-surfaces-order.test.js or a new non-quarantined file).

functional_requirements.description: lib/sd-creation/source-adapters/qf.js:255 born-claims a newly minted SD key via .rpc('claim_sd') with zero stampClaim call — add one, using the existing SD-side stampClaim path (no migration dependency, sdKey there is already an SD key). scripts/qf-start.js:127 makes a genuine QF-id claim_sd call with zero stampClaim call — add one using the FR-2 QF-aware path. Do NOT modify either file's existing pre-checks (gated-hold check, liveness fence, worktree-quota-before-claim ordering in qf-start.js, or the born-claim session/status guards in qf.js) — those are validated, order-dependent fences, not accidental omissions.
functional_requirements.requirement: Add a provenance stamp on the 2 bypassing call sites that never call stampClaim today, without re-routing them through claimGuard().
acceptance_criteria: AC-7: qf.js:255 and qf-start.js:127 each call stampClaim (directly or via a shared helper) immediately after their existing .rpc(claim_sd) success branch, with no change to the surrounding pre-check order.

AC-8: A test on qf-start.js confirms the existing gated-hold refusal (owner=chairman check) and worktree-quota-before-claim ordering are unchanged — stampClaim is added strictly after a successful claim, never before or in place of an existing guard.

functional_requirements.description: isChairmanGatedQF (lib/fleet/qf-gated-hold.cjs:23) must return byte-identical results before and after this SD's changes for the 3 live chairman-gated QF fixtures (QF-20260713-970, QF-20260905-884, QF-20260905-631, as representative shapes) and for a synthetic QF carrying a new pick_reason/provenance field alongside owner/release_condition. This is a proof of non-interference, not a new tripwire script — the review_by/'review_at passed with no dispatch' check named in the SD's original success criteria is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE per the LEAD-corrected scope (validation-agent 787c567b): it would fire on ~0 real rows and duplicates scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs:1953 printChairmanGatedQfs.
functional_requirements.requirement: A unit test proves any chairman-label/provenance data added to a QF row does not alter qf-gated-hold.cjs's existing owner+release_condition hard-exclusion.
acceptance_criteria: AC-9: isChairmanGatedQF(qf) returns true for all 3 live chairman-gated QF fixtures both with and without a pick_reason/provenance field present on the row.
AC-10: isChairmanGatedQF(qf) returns false for a non-gated QF fixture (owner != chairman, or empty release_condition) regardless of whether pick_reason is present.
AC-11: No new script or scheduled check is added for review_by/review_at — confirmed absent from the diff.

functional_requirements.description: Author database/migrations/<date>_add_quick_fixes_metadata.sql: `ALTER TABLE quick_fixes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS metadata jsonb;` (bare JSONB, no DEFAULT, matching the 20260728_add_quick_fix_runtime_observation.sql precedent) with a COMMENT ON COLUMN documenting the pick_reason shape. Per LEAD/PLAN investigation, LEO_MIGRATION_TIER_GATE_BYPASS is disabled (gate ON) so EXEC cannot self-apply this DDL — the migration ships committed-but-unapplied, same posture as the fleet's existing chairman-gated migration backlog. Actually applying it to production is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this child.
functional_requirements.requirement: Ship the additive quick_fixes.metadata migration as chairman-gated/deferred; the code path must work correctly whether or not it has been applied.
acceptance_criteria: AC-12: The migration file exists, is additive-only (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, no data rewrite, no NOT NULL), and follows the repo naming/header convention.

AC-13: With the migration UNAPPLIED, every code path touching quick_fixes.metadata (FR-2) degrades fail-soft with no thrown error, verified by a smoke test running against the live (unapplied) schema.

technical_requirements.rationale: safe-metadata-merge.mjs exists precisely to prevent a read-spread-write race that resurrects a concurrently-cleared flag; claim-stamp.cjs already uses it and must continue to.
technical_requirements.requirement: stampClaim() extension must use the existing mergeMetadataKeys() atomic JSONB partial-key merge for the strategic_directives_v2 path (no full-blob overwrite).

technical_requirements.rationale: Child B (the comparator) ships on a separate branch; Child E must not hard-depend on unmerged code, and must degrade to UNSCORED cleanly when the module lands later.
technical_requirements.requirement: lib/priority/comparator.cjs must be require()'d optionally (try/catch around require, or an existence check) since it is not present on main as of this PRD.

technical_requirements.rationale: TESTING-AGENT FINDING (evidence e21a99e7): stampClaim's existing catch-all makes every failure mode (missing column, network error, malformed patch, genuine bug) return an identical null, so a requirement stated as 'catch 42703 specifically' is unverifiable and trivially satisfiable by the very broad catch it is meant to forbid. The new QF-merge function must surface a distinguishable code/reason on its own return value (not just null) so a caller or test can tell '42703, expected' apart from 'unexpected error, investigate'.
technical_requirements.requirement: The QF-side quick_fixes.metadata write path must catch Postgres error 42703 (undefined_column) by a NAMED, narrow check (error.code === '42703'), never the pre-existing blanket catch{return null} at claim-stamp.cjs:74-76.

technical_requirements.rationale: These were independently validated (validation-agent 787c567b) as intentional, order-dependent design, not drift to be corrected by this SD.
technical_requirements.requirement: No changes to claimGuard()'s call-site set, qf-gated-hold.cjs's predicate logic, or the ordering of pre-claim fences in qf-start.js/session-conflict-checker.mjs/worker-checkin.cjs tryClaim.

technical_requirements.rationale: 14 live consumers of claim_history were enumerated (Explore evidence 0696b09c) and confirmed to be key-addressed/defensive — an additive-only change is the constraint that keeps that guarantee true.
technical_requirements.requirement: CLAIM_HISTORY_CAP (20) and the existing claim_history entry shape (session_id, claimed_at, optional identity_source) are preserved; pick_reason is additive only.

technical_requirements.rationale: TESTING-AGENT FINDING (evidence e21a99e7): typeof NaN === 'number' passes a naive numeric guard, and JSON.stringify(NaN) silently serializes to null, corrupting the stored provenance field with no error. The UNSCORED-fallback check must use Number.isFinite(), not typeof === 'number'.
technical_requirements.requirement: A NaN or non-numeric result from an injected/optional scoring function must never reach JSON.stringify as null or NaN in the stored pick_reason.

system_architecture: {"overview":"A single extension point (stampClaim in lib/fleet/claim-stamp.cjs) grows two new capabilities: (1) it computes and attaches a pick_reason object using an optionally-available scoring module, and (2) it becomes table-aware so a QF-id claim can be stamped onto quick_fixes.metadata once that column exists. Two previously-silent call sites (qf.js, qf-start.js) gain their first-ever stampClaim call. No new services, no new RPC, no new API surface — this is a metadata-provenance layer riding on the existing claim_sd write path.","components":[{"name":"stampClaim (extended)","responsibility":"Builds and merges the claim_history entry, now including pick_reason; dispatches to strategic_directives_v2 or quick_fixes based on an explicit kind/table hint.","technology":"Node.js CJS module (lib/fleet/claim-stamp.cjs)"},{"name":"comparator.cjs (optional dependency)","responsibility":"Supplies computePriorityScore({criticality, alignment, leverage, age}) -> {score, components, comparatorVersion}; plan_checklist.text: SD requirements mapped to technical specs

risks.risk: quick_fixes.metadata migration sits chairman-gated/unapplied indefinitely, so the QF-side pick_reason stamping never actually activates in production.
risks.mitigation: Design the code path to be fully correct and tested in the unapplied state (fail-soft, TS-3/TS-9) so shipping does not depend on migration timing; the SD's success is defined by the code being ready, not by chairman DDL approval, which is explicitly out of scope.
risks.rollback_plan: No rollback needed for the unapplied-migration case since nothing changes in production behavior. If the migration is later applied and causes an unexpected issue, revert via a companion DOWN migration (ALTER TABLE quick_fixes DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS metadata).

risks.risk: A future caller of stampClaim assumes claim_history entries always have a numeric pick_reason.score, breaking on the UNSCORED sentinel string.
risks.mitigation: Document the UNSCORED contract prominently in claim-stamp.cjs's docblock (mirroring comparator.cjs's own documented contract) and cover it with TS-2; any new consumer added later must type-check before arithmetic.
risks.rollback_plan: Revert the pick_reason field addition (feature-flaggable via a simple early-return in stampClaim) if a consumer regression is discovered; the entry shape reverts to the pre-existing 3-key form.

risks.risk: The QF-side CAS-guarded metadata merge, being hand-rolled rather than using a shared helper (none exists for quick_fixes), introduces a subtle race distinct from the SD-side mergeMetadataKeys.
risks.mitigation: Model the QF merge query directly on mergeMetadataKeys' COALESCE(metadata, '{}'::jsonb) || $2::jsonb pattern plus an explicit WHERE claiming_session_id = $sessionId guard, and cover it with a concurrent-write test analogous to tests/unit/fleet/claim-stamp-concurrent-metadata-race.test.js.
risks.rollback_plan: The QF-side write is fail-soft by construction (TS-4); if the race is found post-merge, disable the QF-side write path via a single guard flag while the SD-side path continues unaffected.

# Product Requirements Document

## Strategic Directive
SD-LEO-INFRA-PRIORITY-RECORD-ONE-001-E

## Title
Child E: stamp the pick reason on every claim; reconcile chairman-label provenance with the existing qf-gated-hold.cjs hard-exclusion

## Status
Planning

## Executive Summary
Extend the existing stampClaim() writer to carry a pick_reason (score, components, comparator version) on every claim, make it QF-aware, and prove chairman-label provenance never alters qf-gated-hold.cjs's exclusion.

## Functional Requirements

### FR-1: stampClaim() in lib/fleet/claim-stamp.cjs writes a pick_reason field on the claim_history entry it already appends.
Extend the entry built at claim-stamp.cjs:59-62 with pick_reason: {score, components, comparatorVersion}. Source the values by optional-requiring lib/priority/comparator.cjs (computePriorityScore) — a module that exists on the Child B branch but is not yet merged to main. When the module is absent (require throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND) or its output has no numeric score, pick_reason.score MUST be the literal string 'UNSCORED', never a fabricated 0 (mirrors comparator.cjs's own UNSCORED contract). No changes to CLAIM_HISTORY_CAP (20) or existing entry fields (session_id, claimed_at, identity_source).
**Priority**: CRITICAL
**Acceptance Criteria**:- AC-1: A claim written through claimGuard(), tryClaim() (worker-checkin.cjs), sd-start.js, or session-conflict-checker.mjs produces a claim_history entry whose newest element has a pick_reason object.- AC-2: When lib/priority/comparator.cjs is not present on disk, pick_reason reads {score: "UNSCORED", components: {}, comparatorVersion: null} and stampClaim still returns non-null (fail-soft, not fail-open-to-throw).- AC-3: All 4 existing unit suites referencing claim_history entries (claim-identity.test.js, same-turn-next-claim.test.js, claim-stamp-concurrent-metadata-race.test.js) pass unmodified — pick_reason is additive, asserted via toMatchObject/targeted-key checks, not toEqual on the full entry.

### FR-2: stampClaim() accepts an explicit target-table/kind and, for a QF-id claim, writes to quick_fixes when a metadata column is present, degrading fail-soft (no-op, no throw) when it is absent.
Add a 5th optional parameter (e.g. {kind: 'qf'|'sd'} or auto-detect via the existing QF-id shape check already used elsewhere in the codebase, e.g. sdKey.startsWith('QF-')). For kind='qf', attempt an additive JSONB merge onto quick_fixes.metadata using the SAME atomic read-merge-write discipline as mergeMetadataKeys (a client-side read-then-write is acceptable ONLY behind an explicit compare-and-swap on claiming_session_id, since no generic quick_fixes JSONB merge helper exists in the repo today — do not introduce an unguarded full-blob overwrite). Detect the missing-column case via Postgres error code 42703 and return null without throwing, exactly like the existing qf.factory_lane / qf.verified_at degrade pattern in scripts/worker-checkin.cjs.
**Priority**: HIGH
**Acceptance Criteria**:- AC-4: With quick_fixes.metadata ABSENT (todays live schema), a QF self-claim through worker-checkin.cjs selfClaimQuickFix succeeds end-to-end and stampClaim returns null with no thrown error and no test failure.- AC-5: A unit test with a mocked quick_fixes.metadata column present asserts a pick_reason-bearing entry is written additively (existing metadata keys preserved) under a claiming_session_id compare-and-swap guard.- AC-6: lib/checkin/steps/critical-qf-jump.cjs and lib/checkin/steps/directed-assignment.cjs (the other 2 silent-no-op QF-id claim lanes identified in LEAD/PLAN investigation) route through the same QF-aware stampClaim path, not a separate implementation.

### FR-3: Add a provenance stamp on the 2 bypassing call sites that never call stampClaim today, without re-routing them through claimGuard().
lib/sd-creation/source-adapters/qf.js:255 born-claims a newly minted SD key via .rpc('claim_sd') with zero stampClaim call — add one, using the existing SD-side stampClaim path (no migration dependency, sdKey there is already an SD key). scripts/qf-start.js:127 makes a genuine QF-id claim_sd call with zero stampClaim call — add one using the FR-2 QF-aware path. Do NOT modify either file's existing pre-checks (gated-hold check, liveness fence, worktree-quota-before-claim ordering in qf-start.js, or the born-claim session/status guards in qf.js) — those are validated, order-dependent fences, not accidental omissions.
**Priority**: HIGH
**Acceptance Criteria**:- AC-7: qf.js:255 and qf-start.js:127 each call stampClaim (directly or via a shared helper) immediately after their existing .rpc(claim_sd) success branch, with no change to the surrounding pre-check order.- AC-8: A test on qf-start.js confirms the existing gated-hold refusal (owner=chairman check) and worktree-quota-before-claim ordering are unchanged — stampClaim is added strictly after a successful claim, never before or in place of an existing guard.

### FR-4: A unit test proves any chairman-label/provenance data added to a QF row does not alter qf-gated-hold.cjs's existing owner+release_condition hard-exclusion.
isChairmanGatedQF (lib/fleet/qf-gated-hold.cjs:23) must return byte-identical results before and after this SD's changes for the 3 live chairman-gated QF fixtures (QF-20260713-970, QF-20260905-884, QF-20260905-631, as representative shapes) and for a synthetic QF carrying a new pick_reason/provenance field alongside owner/release_condition. This is a proof of non-interference, not a new tripwire script — the review_by/'review_at passed with no dispatch' check named in the SD's original success criteria is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE per the LEAD-corrected scope (validation-agent 787c567b): it would fire on ~0 real rows and duplicates scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs:1953 printChairmanGatedQfs.
**Priority**: MEDIUM
**Acceptance Criteria**:- AC-9: isChairmanGatedQF(qf) returns true for all 3 live chairman-gated QF fixtures both with and without a pick_reason/provenance field present on the row.- AC-10: isChairmanGatedQF(qf) returns false for a non-gated QF fixture (owner != chairman, or empty release_condition) regardless of whether pick_reason is present.- AC-11: No new script or scheduled check is added for review_by/review_at — confirmed absent from the diff.

### FR-5: Ship the additive quick_fixes.metadata migration as chairman-gated/deferred; the code path must work correctly whether or not it has been applied.
Author database/migrations/<date>_add_quick_fixes_metadata.sql: `ALTER TABLE quick_fixes ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS metadata jsonb;` (bare JSONB, no DEFAULT, matching the 20260728_add_quick_fix_runtime_observation.sql precedent) with a COMMENT ON COLUMN documenting the pick_reason shape. Per LEAD/PLAN investigation, LEO_MIGRATION_TIER_GATE_BYPASS is disabled (gate ON) so EXEC cannot self-apply this DDL — the migration ships committed-but-unapplied, same posture as the fleet's existing chairman-gated migration backlog. Actually applying it to production is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this child.
**Priority**: MEDIUM
**Acceptance Criteria**:- AC-12: The migration file exists, is additive-only (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, no data rewrite, no NOT NULL), and follows the repo naming/header convention.- AC-13: With the migration UNAPPLIED, every code path touching quick_fixes.metadata (FR-2) degrades fail-soft with no thrown error, verified by a smoke test running against the live (unapplied) schema.

## Technical Requirements

### TR-1: stampClaim() extension must use the existing mergeMetadataKeys() atomic JSONB partial-key merge for the strategic_directives_v2 path (no full-blob overwrite).
**Rationale**: safe-metadata-merge.mjs exists precisely to prevent a read-spread-write race that resurrects a concurrently-cleared flag; claim-stamp.cjs already uses it and must continue to.

### TR-2: lib/priority/comparator.cjs must be require()'d optionally (try/catch around require, or an existence check) since it is not present on main as of this PRD.
**Rationale**: Child B (the comparator) ships on a separate branch; Child E must not hard-depend on unmerged code, and must degrade to UNSCORED cleanly when the module lands later.

### TR-3: The QF-side quick_fixes.metadata write path must detect Postgres error 42703 (undefined_column) specifically and treat it as a fail-soft no-op, not a generic catch-and-swallow.
**Rationale**: Mirrors the existing factory_lane/verified_at column-degrade pattern in scripts/worker-checkin.cjs; a broad catch would also hide genuine bugs in the merge query.

### TR-4: No changes to claimGuard()'s call-site set, qf-gated-hold.cjs's predicate logic, or the ordering of pre-claim fences in qf-start.js/session-conflict-checker.mjs/worker-checkin.cjs tryClaim.
**Rationale**: These were independently validated (validation-agent 787c567b) as intentional, order-dependent design, not drift to be corrected by this SD.

### TR-5: CLAIM_HISTORY_CAP (20) and the existing claim_history entry shape (session_id, claimed_at, optional identity_source) are preserved; pick_reason is additive only.
**Rationale**: 14 live consumers of claim_history were enumerated (Explore evidence 0696b09c) and confirmed to be key-addressed/defensive — an additive-only change is the constraint that keeps that guarantee true.

## System Architecture
### Overview
A single extension point (stampClaim in lib/fleet/claim-stamp.cjs) grows two new capabilities: (1) it computes and attaches a pick_reason object using an optionally-available scoring module, and (2) it becomes table-aware so a QF-id claim can be stamped onto quick_fixes.metadata once that column exists. Two previously-silent call sites (qf.js, qf-start.js) gain their first-ever stampClaim call. No new services, no new RPC, no new API surface — this is a metadata-provenance layer riding on the existing claim_sd write path.
### Components
#### stampClaim (extended)- **Responsibility**: Builds and merges the claim_history entry, now including pick_reason; dispatches to strategic_directives_v2 or quick_fixes based on an explicit kind/table hint.- **Technology**: Node.js CJS module (lib/fleet/claim-stamp.cjs)
#### comparator.cjs (optional dependency)- **Responsibility**: Supplies computePriorityScore({criticality, alignment, leverage, age}) -> {score, components, comparatorVersion}; consumed via optional require with UNSCORED fallback.- **Technology**: Node.js CJS module (lib/priority/comparator.cjs, ships on a sibling branch)
#### QF metadata merge path- **Responsibility**: Additive, compare-and-swap-guarded JSONB write onto quick_fixes.metadata; fail-soft on missing column (42703).- **Technology**: Supabase-js client + raw pg fallback for the JSONB merge, mirroring safe-metadata-merge.mjs conventions
#### quick_fixes.metadata migration- **Responsibility**: Additive schema change enabling the QF metadata merge path once chairman-applied.- **Technology**: PostgreSQL migration file (chairman-gated tier)
#### qf-gated-hold non-interference test- **Responsibility**: Regression-proves isChairmanGatedQF is unaffected by any new provenance field.- **Technology**: Vitest unit test
### Data Flow
A caller (claimGuard, tryClaim, sd-start.js, session-conflict-checker.mjs, qf.js, or qf-start.js) succeeds at .rpc('claim_sd') → calls the extended stampClaim(supabase, ref, sessionId, identitySource, {kind}) → stampClaim reads the current row (strategic_directives_v2 or quick_fixes depending on kind) → computes pick_reason via optional comparator.cjs → appends {session_id, claimed_at, identity_source, pick_reason} to claim_history (capped at 20) → writes back via an atomic partial-key JSONB merge (mergeMetadataKeys for SD; an equivalent CAS-guarded merge for QF) → returns the entry or null on any fail-soft condition.
### Integration Points- lib/coordinator/safe-metadata-merge.mjs (reused for the SD-side atomic merge)- lib/priority/comparator.cjs (optional; Child B branch)- lib/fleet/qf-gated-hold.cjs (read-only regression target, not modified)- scripts/worker-checkin.cjs (3 QF-id claim lanes: selfClaimQuickFix, critical-qf-jump.cjs, directed-assignment.cjs)- lib/sd-creation/source-adapters/qf.js and scripts/qf-start.js (2 new stampClaim call sites)

## Implementation Approach
### Phases
#### Phase 1: SD-side pick_reasonExtend stampClaim() to compute and attach pick_reason using an optionally-required comparator.cjs; extend all 4 existing unit suites to assert additive behavior.
**Deliverables**:- lib/fleet/claim-stamp.cjs extended- New/updated unit tests for TS-1, TS-2, TS-6
#### Phase 2: QF-awareness + migrationAdd the table/kind parameter to stampClaim, implement the CAS-guarded QF metadata merge with 42703 fail-soft, author the additive migration file.
**Deliverables**:- stampClaim QF-aware extension- database migration file (unapplied)- Unit tests for TS-3, TS-4, TS-9
#### Phase 3: Bypass-site provenance + gated-hold regressionAdd stampClaim calls to qf.js:255 and qf-start.js:127; write the qf-gated-hold non-interference regression test.
**Deliverables**:- qf.js and qf-start.js updated- Tests for TS-7, TS-8, TS-5
### Key Technical Decisions- Extend the existing stampClaim() writer rather than build a new one, per the LEAD-corrected premise that a single writer already exists (validation-agent 787c567b).- Do not re-route the 3 bypassing claim_sd call sites through claimGuard() — their pre-checks are validated as intentional, order-dependent fencing.- Ship the quick_fixes.metadata migration as chairman-gated/deferred rather than block this SD on chairman DDL approval; code degrades fail-soft until applied.- Drop the review_by/review_at tripwire from scope — it would fire on ~0 real rows and duplicates an existing fleet-dashboard.cjs surface.

## Test Scenarios

### TS-1: SD claim through claimGuard() stamps pick_reason using a present comparator.cjs
**Type**: unit
**Given**: lib/priority/comparator.cjs is present and returns a numeric score for given inputs
**When**: claimGuard() successfully claims an SD
**Then**: the newest claim_history entry has pick_reason.score as a number and comparatorVersion matching comparator.cjs's COMPARATOR_VERSION

### TS-2: SD claim stamps UNSCORED when comparator.cjs is absent
**Type**: unit
**Given**: lib/priority/comparator.cjs cannot be required (module not found, simulated via a test double)
**When**: tryClaim() in worker-checkin.cjs successfully claims an SD
**Then**: the newest claim_history entry has pick_reason.score === "UNSCORED", and stampClaim does not throw

### TS-3: QF self-claim succeeds when quick_fixes.metadata column is absent (todays live schema)
**Type**: integration
**Given**: quick_fixes.metadata column does not exist (live production shape)
**When**: selfClaimQuickFix() in worker-checkin.cjs claims an open QF
**Then**: the claim succeeds, stampClaim returns null for the QF-side write, and no error propagates to the caller

### TS-4: QF metadata merge is additive under a mocked present column
**Type**: unit
**Given**: a mocked quick_fixes row with an existing metadata blob {foo: "bar"} and a present metadata column
**When**: the QF-aware stampClaim path runs for that row
**Then**: the resulting metadata contains both foo: "bar" (preserved) and the new pick_reason-bearing claim_history-equivalent entry, under a claiming_session_id CAS guard

### TS-5: qf-gated-hold exclusion is unaffected by a new provenance field
**Type**: unit
**Given**: a QF fixture with owner="chairman" and a non-empty release_condition, plus a new pick_reason/provenance field
**When**: isChairmanGatedQF(qf) is called
**Then**: it returns true, identically to the same fixture without the new field

### TS-6: Existing claim_history consumers tolerate the new key
**Type**: unit
**Given**: the 4 existing unit suites referencing claim_history (claim-identity.test.js, same-turn-next-claim.test.js, claim-stamp-concurrent-metadata-race.test.js, and any effort-experiment reader tests)
**When**: run against the extended stampClaim output
**Then**: all suites pass unmodified

### TS-7: qf.js born-claim now stamps provenance
**Type**: unit
**Given**: a QF worker session with a matching sd_key === qf.id, live status
**When**: the escalation born-claims a newly minted SD via qf.js:255
**Then**: stampClaim is called and the SD's claim_history gains a pick_reason-bearing entry, with no change to the existing session/status guard logic

### TS-8: qf-start.js claim now stamps provenance without disturbing gate ordering
**Type**: integration
**Given**: a QF that is NOT chairman-gated and passes the liveness fence and worktree-quota check
**When**: qf-start.js claims it
**Then**: the claim succeeds, stampClaim is called after the quota check (never before), and a chairman-gated QF is still refused exactly as before this change

### TS-9: Migration is additive and safe to leave unapplied
**Type**: integration
**Given**: the quick_fixes.metadata migration file has NOT been applied to the live database
**When**: the full test suite and a live self-claim smoke test run
**Then**: no test fails due to the missing column, and no error surfaces to a worker

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A claim written through every one of the 6 production claim_sd call sites (claimGuard, session-conflict-checker.mjs, worker-checkin.cjs tryClaim, sd-start.js, lib/sd-creation/source-adapters/qf.js, scripts/qf-start.js) results in a pick_reason-bearing claim_history/metadata entry, or a documented, tested fail-soft no-op for the QF-metadata path while the migration is unapplied.
2. isChairmanGatedQF (lib/fleet/qf-gated-hold.cjs) is provably unaffected by any new provenance field, confirmed by a passing regression test against all 3 live chairman-gated QF fixtures.
3. All existing claim_history/stampClaim unit tests pass unmodified; no reader of claim_history breaks.
4. The quick_fixes.metadata migration exists, is additive-only, and the codebase functions correctly whether it is applied or not.
5. No re-routing of the 3 already-bypassing claim_sd call sites through claimGuard(), and no new review_by/review_at tripwire script — both explicitly out of scope per the LEAD-corrected scope.

## Risks & Mitigations

### quick_fixes.metadata migration sits chairman-gated/unapplied indefinitely, so the QF-side pick_reason stamping never actually activates in production.
**Probability**: MEDIUM
**Impact**: MEDIUM
**Mitigation**: Design the code path to be fully correct and tested in the unapplied state (fail-soft, TS-3/TS-9) so shipping does not depend on migration timing; the SD's success is defined by the code being ready, not by chairman DDL approval, which is explicitly out of scope.
**Rollback Plan**: No rollback needed for the unapplied-migration case since nothing changes in production behavior. If the migration is later applied and causes an unexpected issue, revert via a companion DOWN migration (ALTER TABLE quick_fixes DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS metadata).

### A future caller of stampClaim assumes claim_history entries always have a numeric pick_reason.score, breaking on the UNSCORED sentinel string.
**Probability**: LOW
**Impact**: MEDIUM
**Mitigation**: Document the UNSCORED contract prominently in claim-stamp.cjs's docblock (mirroring comparator.cjs's own documented contract) and cover it with TS-2; any new consumer added later must type-check before arithmetic.
**Rollback Plan**: Revert the pick_reason field addition (feature-flaggable via a simple early-return in stampClaim) if a consumer regression is discovered; the entry shape reverts to the pre-existing 3-key form.

### The QF-side CAS-guarded metadata merge, being hand-rolled rather than using a shared helper (none exists for quick_fixes), introduces a subtle race distinct from the SD-side mergeMetadataKeys.
**Probability**: LOW
**Impact**: HIGH
**Mitigation**: Model the QF merge query directly on mergeMetadataKeys' COALESCE(metadata, '{}'::jsonb) || $2::jsonb pattern plus an explicit WHERE claiming_session_id = $sessionId guard, and cover it with a concurrent-write test analogous to tests/unit/fleet/claim-stamp-concurrent-metadata-race.test.js.
**Rollback Plan**: The QF-side write is fail-soft by construction (TS-4); if the race is found post-merge, disable the QF-side write path via a single guard flag while the SD-side path continues unaffected.

consumers.name: Coordinator weekly review / SRE audit
consumers.interaction: Reads claim_history[].pick_reason to audit whether top-ranked picks advanced the wave (MOVED-THE-NUMBER rate), per the parent SD chairman ruling.

consumers.name: Every fleet worker session (via tryClaim/claimGuard/sd-start.js)
consumers.interaction: Triggers stampClaim as a side effect of a normal claim; no direct interaction required.

dependencies.name: lib/priority/comparator.cjs (Child B)
dependencies.contract: Optional require; computePriorityScore(item, inputs) -> {score, components, comparatorVersion}
dependencies.failure_handling: Module absent or throws -> pick_reason.score = "UNSCORED", no error propagates.

dependencies.name: quick_fixes.metadata column (chairman-gated migration)
dependencies.failure_handling: Column absent (42703) -> QF-side stamp is a no-op, claim still succeeds.

data_contracts.schema: { score: number | "UNSCORED", components: Record<string, number|"UNSCORED">, comparatorVersion: string|null }
data_contracts.validation: Unit-tested shape assertions (TS-1, TS-2); no DB-level CHECK constraint (JSONB sub-shape, matching existing claim_history convention).
data_contracts.versioning: comparatorVersion field carries the source formula version forward for future audit.

runtime_config.deployment_considerations: No deployment-time flag needed; the fail-soft design means the code is safe to ship regardless of migration state.

monitoring: Count of claim_history entries carrying a numeric (non-UNSCORED) pick_reason.score over time, as a proxy for comparator.cjs adoption once Child B merges.
observability_rollout.rollback_trigger: A regression in any of the 4 existing claim_history unit suites, or a production claim failure traced to the pick_reason extension.
observability_rollout.rollout_strategy: Direct merge — additive-only change with fail-soft degradation, no phased rollout required.
observability_rollout.rollback_procedure: Revert the stampClaim extension commit; claim_history reverts to its pre-existing 3-key entry shape with no data loss (pick_reason was purely additive).
